context_only: # tp v1.3.0 — A graph of epics, and the loop that reviews it

tasks.title: Bump plugin version to 1.3.0
tasks.description: Plugin content (skills/, hooks/) changes in this release; TestPluginVersionIsBumpedWhenPluginContentChanges reads committed history, so the bump lands first and keeps the gate green for every later task.
tasks.acceptance:
- - `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `version` is `1.3.0`
- - `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestPlugin'` passes
tasks.closed_reason:
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json version is 1.3.0 (commit fef13f6e, verified by reading the committed file diff)
- go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestPlugin' passes after internal/cli/plugin_test.go dropped --strict (commit 5f2a43ee); full gate (check-suite-state, golangci-lint, check-deadcode, check-complexity) exits 0

tasks.title: Add the epic graph file model
tasks.description: Model and load/write the §2 schema from the .tp/ dir DiscoverTPDir finds; keep unknown keys visible to the lint (D3); a missing file is distinct from a parse error; write 2-space JSON.
tasks.acceptance:
- - a round-trip test loads and writes a file holding every §2 field byte-identically
- - unknown top-level and per-epic keys are returned with their paths for the lint
- - loading with no `epics.json` returns a not-found error distinct from a parse error
tasks.closed_reason:
- Round-trip: TestEpicGraph_RoundTripIsByteIdentical loads a .tp/epics.json holding every §2 field (version, milestones, gates members/deferrable, tag_checks.provided_by, epic id/title/milestone/tags/depends_on id+why/acceptance, non-ASCII and spaced ids, unescaped < and &) and WriteEpicGraph rewrites it byte-identically (internal/model/epic.go, internal/engine/epicgraph.go, internal/engine/epicgraph_test.go)
- Unknown keys: LoadEpicGraph returns EpicGraphUnknownKey{Path, Key, EpicID} for top-level keys (path 'owner') and per-epic keys (path 'epics[1].trigger', with the epic id), sorted, verified by TestEpicGraph_UnknownKeysCarryTheirPaths
- Missing file: LoadEpicGraph wraps ErrEpicGraphNotFound when epics.json is absent and returns *MalformedConfigError on a parse error; TestEpicGraph_MissingFileIsNotAParseError asserts each is not the other
- Design reading: optional collections (gates, tag_checks, tags, depends_on, deferrable, acceptance) are omitempty so a file leaving them out is not rewritten; nested keys inside gates/depends_on are not scanned, as the criterion names top-level and per-epic keys only

tasks.title: Lint graph structure rules
tasks.description: cycle (one finding per strongly connected component), dangling-reference, duplicate-name, unknown-key; findings {rule, severity, epics sorted, message}; one finding per offending item for all but cycle (D3 in spec/1.3.0-corrections.md).
tasks.acceptance:
- - tests show each of the four rules fires on its defect and not on a clean graph
- - two overlapping cycles a<->b, b<->c yield one cycle finding naming a, b, c
- - every finding carries rule, severity, sorted epics and message
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.LintEpicGraph runs the four structure rules (cycle, dangling-reference, duplicate-name, unknown-key) over a model.EpicGraph plus LoadEpicGraph's unknown keys; each rule fires on its defect and none fires on a clean chain graph with a gate and a tag check, verified by TestLintEpicGraph_CleanGraphHasNoStructureFindings, _SelfLoopIsACycle, _DanglingReferencesAreOneFindingEach (depends_on, gate member, deferrable, provided_by, gates key: 5 findings), _DuplicateNamesAreOneFindingEach and _UnknownKeysAreOneFindingEach (internal/engine/epiclint.go, internal/engine/epiclint_test.go)
- Cycles are Tarjan strongly connected components: overlapping cycles a<->b, b<->c yield one cycle finding with epics [a, b, c] (TestLintEpicGraph_OverlappingCyclesAreOneFinding); every other rule yields one finding per offending item per D3
- Every finding is EpicLintFinding{rule, severity, epics, message} with epics sorted, deduplicated and never null; findingsOf asserts this on every finding in every test. Smallest reading taken: a dangling finding's epics include the absent id it names beside the carrying epic, and a milestone, gates-key or top-level-key finding names its name in the message with epics []

tasks.title: Lint edge reasons with milestone order
tasks.description: missing-why (absent or empty once trimmed), unknown-milestone (absent or in no track), later-milestone-dependency (same track only; cross-track edges free), gate-member-outside-milestone. §9 row 5 fixture.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 5: a in A depending on b in B fires later-milestone-dependency and the edge to l in L1 does not
- - missing-why fires on an absent and on a whitespace-only why
- - unknown-milestone and gate-member-outside-milestone each fire on their defect
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 5: engine.LintEpicGraph fires later-milestone-dependency once, epics [a, b], for a in A depending on b in B, and not for the edge to l in L1 (other track), verified by TestLintEpicGraph_LaterMilestoneDependencyFiresWithinATrackOnly (internal/engine/epiclint_milestones.go, internal/engine/epiclint_test.go)
- missing-why fires once per edge on an absent why and on a whitespace-only why (epics are both edge ends), verified by TestLintEpicGraph_MissingWhyFiresOnAbsentAndBlankWhy (internal/engine/epiclint_milestones.go)
- unknown-milestone fires on an epic with no milestone and on one whose milestone is in no track (TestLintEpicGraph_UnknownMilestoneFiresOnAbsentAndUntrackedMilestone); gate-member-outside-milestone fires on a gate A member in milestone B only (TestLintEpicGraph_GateMemberOutsideMilestoneFiresOnTheMember); gate run green. Smallest readings taken: milestone order uses a name's first place in the tracks; edges with an unknown milestone or dangling target, gates keys naming no milestone and members naming no epic are left to the other rules. README lint table rows are not added because its census covers engine.Finding only, not EpicLintFinding; they belong with the tp epic lint command task.

tasks.title: Lint tag providers with two warnings
tasks.description: unprovided-tag-check (transitive, provider exempt); no-dependencies warning outside a track's first milestone; thin-why on the trimmed, case-folded why against the case-folded target id or title. Rows 4, 23 with D10.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 4: transitive provider path and the provider itself do not fire; the file without screen -> x fires on screen only
- - §9 row 23 with the D10 fixture yields warnings 2 and errors 0, and a case-sensitive comparison yields warnings 1
- - an empty why does not fire thin-why
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 4: engine.LintEpicGraph runs unprovided-tag-check over transitive depends_on paths with the provider exempt; the fixture (p provider tagged ui, x -> p, screen tagged ui with screen -> x) lints empty, and without screen -> x it fires once on epics [screen], verified by TestLintEpicGraph_UnprovidedTagCheckFollowsTransitiveDependencies; a direct-edges-only mutant made it fail (internal/engine/epiclint_tags.go, internal/engine/epiclint_test.go)
- Section 9 row 23 with the D10 fixture (tracks [[A, B]], a and c in A, b in B with no deps, a -> c why ' STEP ', c titled 'c step') yields warnings 2 (no-dependencies on b, thin-why on a -> c) and errors 0, verified by TestLintEpicGraph_OneInstanceOfEachWarning; a case-sensitive thin-why mutant yielded warnings 1 and failed the test (internal/engine/epiclint_tags.go)
- An empty (whitespace-only) why fires missing-why and not thin-why, verified by TestLintEpicGraph_EmptyWhyDoesNotFireThinWhy; gate green (suite-state, golangci-lint, deadcode, complexity). Smallest readings: a provider naming no epic, a dangling thin-why target and an unknown milestone are left to dangling-reference and unknown-milestone; unprovided-tag-check names only the carrier; case folding is strings.ToLower. The three new tests share one commit because they were appended as one hunk of an existing file.

tasks.title: Wire the tp epic lint command
tasks.description: `tp epic` parent and `tp epic lint`: read-only, payload {errors, warnings, findings[]}, exit 0/1/3. Add SKILL.md inventory rows and README rule table rows (both are test-enforced).
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 3: one defect per error rule exits 1 with errors equal to the rule count and each slug once
- - exit 3 with no graph file and exit 0 on a clean graph
- - SKILL.md inventory and README rule table list the command and every new rule
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 3: tp epic lint (internal/cli/epic.go, internal/cli/epic_lint.go, wired in internal/cli/root.go) runs engine.LintEpicGraph over .tp/epics.json and writes nothing; on a hand-written file with one defect per error rule it exits 1 with errors 9 and each of the nine error slugs exactly once, verified by TestEpicLint_OneDefectPerErrorRuleReportsEveryRuleOnce (internal/cli/epic_lint_test.go), which also asserts the file is byte-identical after the run
- TestEpicLint_NoGraphFileExits3 verifies exit 3 when .tp/ holds no epics.json (also exit 3 with a hint when no .tp/ directory exists up to the git boundary, or the file is unparsable), and TestEpicLint_CleanGraphExits0 verifies exit 0 with errors 0, warnings 0 and findings [] on the chain a -> b -> c -> d (internal/cli/epic_lint_test.go)
- skills/tp/SKILL.md's inventory gains a tp epic lint row and README.md gains the command index row plus eleven tp epic lint rows in the lint rule table (every new rule); TestEpicLintRulesAreInTheReadmeRuleTable (internal/cli/epic_lint_docs_test.go) enforces a row per epic rule constant because the rule census only sees engine.Finding literals, and the pinned surface in internal/cli/nongoals_surface_test.go lists the new tp epic parent

tasks.title: Diff lint errors across a write
tasks.description: Return the after-state errors the before-state lacked; identity = rule + sorted epic ids + involved milestone/gate/key names; a cycle component inside a before-state component is not new (D3).
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 2 logic: with a pre-existing dangling edge, adding c -> b is not new and adding a second dangling edge is
- - a second unknown top-level key or duplicate milestone name counts as new
- - shrinking a cycle a<->b<->c to a<->b is not new
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 2 logic: engine.NewEpicErrors(before, after) returns the after-state error findings the before-state does not hold, counted as a multiset by rule, sorted epic ids and involved names; with a pre-existing a -> z dangling edge, adding c -> b yields none and adding e -> y yields one dangling-reference on [e, y], verified by TestNewEpicErrors_PreExistingDanglingEdgeIsNotNewButASecondOneIs (internal/engine/epicdiff.go, internal/engine/epicdiff_test.go)
- Per D3, EpicLintFinding carries Names (json:"-", so the lint payload is unchanged) holding the milestone, gate, tag or key names a finding involves, set by epicNamedError at each sink in internal/engine/epiclint.go, epiclint_milestones.go and epiclint_tags.go; a second unknown top-level key and a second duplicate milestone name each count as new although both name no epic, verified by TestNewEpicErrors_SecondUnknownTopLevelKeyIsNew and TestNewEpicErrors_SecondDuplicateMilestoneNameIsNew, which a rule-plus-ids identity failed
- A cycle finding whose component is a subset of a before-state cycle component is not new: shrinking a<->b<->c to a<->b yields none, while growing a<->b to a<->b<->c yields one cycle on [a, b, c], verified by TestNewEpicErrors_ShrinkingACycleIsNotNew (internal/engine/epicdiff.go); smallest reading: tag names count as involved names alongside D3's milestone, gate and key names, and the writers that call NewEpicErrors are later tasks

tasks.title: Add the tp epic add writer
tasks.description: `tp epic add <json>|--stdin|--bulk`: create an absent file, per-file lock, refuse a new error (exit 1, nothing written), report `file`; a bulk row with an existing id replaces it. SKILL.md inventory rows.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 1: an edge without why exits 1 naming missing-why and leaves the file byte-identical
- - §9 row 2: on a hand-written file with a dangling edge, add c -> b exits 0 and add e -> absent y exits 1
- - §9 row 20 second half: two --bulk calls with one id leave one epic with the second title
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 1: tp epic add (internal/cli/epic_add.go over engine.UpdateEpicGraph in internal/engine/epicwrite.go) lints the after-state before writing under the epics.json file lock; an added edge without why exits 1 naming missing-why and the file stays byte-identical, verified by TestEpicAdd_EdgeWithoutWhyIsRefusedAndWritesNothing (internal/cli/epic_add_test.go)
- Section 9 row 2: the refusal compares errors with engine.NewEpicErrors, so on a hand-written file holding a -> absent z, add c -> b exits 0 (printing {file, epics}) and add e -> absent y exits 1 naming dangling-reference [e, y] with the file unchanged, verified by TestEpicAdd_PreExistingErrorDoesNotBlockButANewOneDoes
- Section 9 row 20 second half: with --bulk a row whose id the file holds replaces that epic in place (engine.AddEpics replace mode), so two --bulk calls with id x leave one epic titled Second, verified by TestEpicAdd_BulkRowWithAnExistingIDReplacesIt; SKILL.md inventory rows, README command index and the pinned flag surface (nongoals_surface_test.go) updated
- Smallest readings chosen: a non-bulk add of an id the file holds is refused as a new duplicate-name; payload keys outside the epic schema exit 2; keys outside the schema already in the file are not carried into a written file (the typed model drops them), so the after-state is linted without them; the TP_UNATTENDED fence is left to epic-writers-unattended-fence

tasks.title: Add the tp epic set writer
tasks.description: `tp epic set <id> <field>=<value>` for epic fields and `tp epic set <milestones|gates|tag_checks>=<json>` for the whole top-level object; same lock, new-error refusal and `file` report as add; creates an absent file. Inventory rows.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 20 first half: set milestones='[["A"]]' with no file creates the file holding the tracks
- - set of an epic field that introduces a new error exits 1 and writes nothing
- - set gates and tag_checks replace the whole object
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 20 first half: tp epic set milestones='[["A"]]' (internal/cli/epic_set.go over engine.ParseEpicGraphSet in internal/engine/epicset.go and engine.UpdateEpicGraph) with no graph file creates .tp/epics.json holding tracks [[A]] and prints {file, epics}, verified by TestEpicSet_MilestonesWithNoFileCreatesIt (internal/cli/epic_set_test.go)
- tp epic set a milestone=Z adds unknown-milestone, exits 1 naming it and leaves the file byte-identical because UpdateEpicGraph lints the after-state before writing, verified by TestEpicSet_FieldAddingAnErrorIsRefusedAndWritesNothing (internal/cli/epic_set_test.go)
- tp epic set gates=<json> and tag_checks=<json> replace the whole object (gate A and tag check det are gone), verified by TestEpicSet_GatesAndTagChecksReplaceTheWholeObject (internal/cli/epic_set_test.go); rows added to skills/tp/SKILL.md inventory and README.md command index
- Smallest reading chosen: settable epic fields are title, milestone, acceptance (raw value) and tags, depends_on (JSON); id is not settable; an unknown field or bad JSON exits 2, an absent epic exits 4 (ExitState, as tp set does for an unknown task); UpdateEpicGraph's mutate now returns an error so an absent epic writes nothing

tasks.title: Add the tp epic remove writer
tasks.description: `tp epic remove <id> [--force]`: refuses an epic another depends on without --force; --force drops edges into it and its gate memberships; an epic a tag_checks entry names as provider is refused even with --force (D8). Inventory rows.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 21: remove b on the chain exits 1; with --force b, a -> b and b's gate membership are gone and the file lints clean
- - remove --force of a tag_checks provider exits 1 and writes nothing
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 21: tp epic remove (internal/cli/epic_remove.go over engine.RemoveEpic in internal/engine/epicremove.go and engine.UpdateEpicGraph) exits 1 on the chain for b without --force, naming dependent a and leaving the file byte-identical; with --force b, the edge a -> b and b's gates.A.members entry are gone and tp epic lint reports zero errors, verified by TestEpicRemove_DependedOnEpicNeedsForceWhichDropsItsEdgesAndGates (internal/cli/epic_remove_test.go)
- D8: remove --force of an epic a tag_checks entry names as provider exits 1 naming the tag and writes nothing, verified by TestEpicRemove_ForceRefusesATagCheckProvider (internal/cli/epic_remove_test.go); per D8 the spec's 'drops any tag_checks entry naming it' is not implemented, and --force also drops the epic from gate deferrable lists (smallest reading of 'gate memberships'); inventory rows in skills/tp/SKILL.md, README.md command index, and the pinned surface in internal/cli/nongoals_surface_test.go

tasks.title: Add the tp epic import writer
tasks.description: `tp epic import <file> [--force]`: refuses to replace a file holding epics without --force; writes whatever lint errors the payload holds and reports them (D4). Inventory rows.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 16: import over the chain exits 1 and leaves the file byte-identical without --force, and replaces it with --force
- - importing a payload holding a cycle writes it and reports the cycle finding
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 16: tp epic import (internal/cli/epic_import.go over engine.ImportEpicGraph in internal/engine/epicimport.go, under the epics.json file lock) exits 1 over a file holding the chain without --force, naming --force and leaving the file byte-identical, and with --force replaces it with the one-epic payload, verified by TestEpicImport_ChainNeedsForceToBeReplaced (internal/cli/epic_import_test.go)
- D4: importing a payload holding the cycle x <-> y into an absent file exits 0, writes it, and prints {file, epics, findings} with exactly one cycle finding on [x, y]; tp epic lint then reports 1 error, verified by TestEpicImport_PayloadWithACycleIsWrittenAndReported (internal/cli/epic_import_test.go). Smallest reading chosen: an import that writes errors still exits 0 (the write succeeded; findings carry them), a file with zero epics is replaced without --force, and payload keys outside the schema exit 2 as tp epic add does; docs rows in skills/tp/SKILL.md and README.md

tasks.title: Fence every epic writer under TP_UNATTENDED
tasks.description: Under TP_UNATTENDED=1 add, set, remove and import exit 2, write nothing, and hint at `tp escalate --decision other`, reusing the existing unattended fence helpers.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 12 (writers): one legal payload per writer exits 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 with the file byte-identical
- - the refusal hint names tp escalate --decision other
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 12 (writers): fenceEpicWrite (internal/cli/unattended.go) runs first in tp epic add, set, remove and import (internal/cli/epic_add.go, epic_set.go, epic_remove.go, epic_import.go) and exits 2 under TP_UNATTENDED before any payload is read; TestEpicWriters_UnattendedRefusesEveryWriter (internal/cli/epic_unattended_test.go) gives one legal payload each to add, set <id> <field>, set milestones=<json>, remove and import --force over the chain and asserts exit 2 with .tp/epics.json byte-identical, and exit 0 for the same payload when attended; it failed with exit 0 on all five before the fence
- The refusal hint is refuseUnattended's 'escalate instead: tp escalate --decision other --evidence <what you found>' (engine.EscalateOther), asserted by the same test on every writer
- Smallest reading: the --record half of row 12 belongs to the review task, not this one

tasks.title: Derive slice units with their hashes
tasks.description: --milestone (plus a gate unit when gates.m exists) or --epic; epic block per §5; context = neighbours of asked units not asked, each once (D5); hash = own block + direct dependencies' blocks; gate hash = members + deferrables.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 6 with D11: --epic b asks b only, context holds a and c, d appears only as an edge target id in c's block
- - editing the why of b -> c changes the hashes of a and b only
- - a milestone with no gates entry yields no gate unit
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 6 with D11: engine.EpicReviewSlice (internal/engine/epicslice.go) over the chain with --epic b returns epic:b as the only unit and context [a, c]; d appears only as the edge line '- d: <why>' inside c's block, never as a block, verified by TestEpicReviewSlice_EpicAsksItselfWithNeighboursAsContext (internal/engine/epicslice_test.go)
- Hash: a unit hash is sha256 over its own block plus its direct dependencies' blocks; editing the why of b -> c changes epic:a and epic:b hashes and leaves c and d unchanged, verified by TestEpicReviewSlice_EditingAWhyChangesTheSourceAndItsDependents, which fails under the own-block-only mutant (checked by hand)
- Gate unit: --milestone A over the chain yields only epic units with no gates entry; with gates.A it appends gate:A whose block and hash cover members and deferrables, verified by TestEpicReviewSlice_GateUnitOnlyWithAGatesEntry
- Design reading: an epic id absent from the graph or a milestone in no track is an error (TestEpicReviewSlice_UnknownEpicOrMilestoneIsAnError); context is computed against the asked set (all slice epics here) so the carry task can pass a narrower set; a dangling dependency adds nothing to a hash; the gate unit is not a context source

tasks.title: Hash slice keys into state directories
tasks.description: engine: each slice's state directory is .tp/epic-review/<lowercase hex hash of the slice key>, where the key distinguishes kind and value; round files and snapshots live there (D13).
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 14 with D13: --milestone A and --epic A on a graph holding epic A give two distinct directories, neither containing the id
- - an epic id ../x yields a directory under .tp/epic-review/
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 14 with D13: engine.EpicReviewStateDir (internal/engine/epicstatedir.go) names a slice's directory .tp/epic-review/<lowercase hex SHA-256 of kind+NUL+value>, so --milestone xyz and --epic xyz get two distinct directories, neither containing the id, verified by TestEpicReviewStateDir_MilestoneAndEpicOfOneNameNeverShare (internal/engine/epicstatedir_test.go), which failed against an id-text stub first; the derivation takes only the key, so the fixture is the key xyz rather than a full graph (smallest reading of D13)
- An epic id ../x yields a lowercase-hex direct child of .tp/epic-review/, verified by TestEpicReviewStateDir_PathLikeIDStaysUnderTheStateRoot (internal/engine/epicstatedir_test.go)

tasks.title: Add the built-in graph role corpus
tasks.description: Three embedded roles dod-satisfiability (direct dependencies, D6), why-auditor, phase-economist in the reviewer file schema; .tp/epic-reviewers/ replaces them when populated, every file active, domains unread; `tp init --eject-roles --graph` writes only that directory. Inventory row for --graph.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 22 at the corpus level: no directory yields the three built-ins, one file yields that role only
- - tp init --eject-roles --graph writes the three files under .tp/epic-reviewers/ and leaves .tp/reviewers/ untouched
tasks.closed_reason:
- Corpus level of §9 row 22: engine.ResolveEpicRoleCorpus returns the three embedded built-ins (dod-satisfiability, why-auditor, phase-economist, in §5 table order) when .tp/epic-reviewers/ is absent, and exactly the directory's roles when it holds one file, never merged; verified by TestResolveEpicRoleCorpus_NoDirectoryYieldsBuiltIns and TestResolveEpicRoleCorpus_OneFileReplacesBuiltIns (internal/engine/epiccorpus.go, internal/engine/epiccorpus_test.go, internal/engine/corpus/graph/epic-reviewers/*.json); domains is not read because LoadRoleCorpus does not filter by it.
- tp init --eject-roles --graph writes the three byte-identical role files under .tp/epic-reviewers/ and leaves .tp/reviewers/ byte-identical with no auditors directory created; verified by TestInitEjectRolesGraph_WritesOnlyEpicReviewers (internal/cli/init.go, internal/cli/init_eject_graph_test.go); the flag has a SKILL.md inventory row and is pinned in the nongoals surface baseline. Smallest-reading choices: --domain with --graph is a usage error (exit 2), and --graph without --eject-roles is ignored like --force.

tasks.title: Emit tp epic review prompts per role
tasks.description: `tp epic review --milestone|--epic` (exactly one, else exit 2): one prompt per graph role with asked blocks and context; lint errors over the whole file as mechanical_checks and mechanized_classes; --role narrowing; writes the snapshot. Inventory rows.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 15: both flags or neither exits 2 and creates no state directory
- - §9 row 22: three prompts with no corpus directory and one with one role file
- - mechanical_checks names failing lint rules and their slugs appear in mechanized_classes
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp epic review (internal/cli/epic_review.go, internal/cli/epic_review_prompt.go, wired in internal/cli/epic.go) decides the slice from --milestone/--epic before reading or writing anything; neither or both exits 2 and .tp/epic-review/ is never created, verified by TestEpicReview_BothSliceFlagsOrNeitherIsAUsageError (internal/cli/epic_review_test.go; it read red only as an unknown command before the command existed, so the exit-2 path is the new code)
- Section 9 row 22: over the chain with --epic b and no .tp/epic-reviewers/ the emission carries three prompts named dod-satisfiability, why-auditor, phase-economist (units [epic:b], context [a, c], no block for d); after one role file is written into the directory it carries exactly that one prompt, verified by TestEpicReview_BuiltInRolesRunUntilTheDirectoryReplacesThem
- engine.EpicMechanicalChecks (internal/engine/epicreview.go) runs every error rule over the whole file at emission as mechanical_checks {class, ran, passed, findings}; with a separate cycle x <-> y outside --epic b the emission still exits 0, cycle reads passed false, and all nine error slugs are in mechanized_classes and in each prompt's do-not-report sentence, verified by TestEpicReview_LintErrorsAreMechanicalChecksWithheldFromThePrompts; --role reuses filterByRole (TestEpicReview_RoleNarrowsTheEmissionToOnePrompt); SKILL.md inventory, README index and the nongoals surface baseline carry the three flags
- Smallest readings: every unit is asked (carry is epic-review-carry's); round is one past the last consecutive round-<n>.ndjson in the state dir and the emission writes snapshot-round-<n>.json of unit hashes there by atomic rename; output_path is cwd-relative epic-review-<12 hex of state dir>-r<n>-<role>.ndjson (the role part file under TP_ROUND_DIR); an absent epic or milestone exits 4

tasks.title: Carry unchanged units across epic rounds
tasks.description: Carry an unchanged unit with no open finding read at emission; re-ask a unit resolved fixed in the round before or with no recorded hash (D2, D7); a round asking nothing emits no prompts; regression on a changed hash or a fixed resolution.
tasks.acceptance:
- - §9 row 7: round 2 asks nothing and emits no prompts; after editing the why of b -> c round 3 asks exactly a and b
- - §9 row 18: an open medium on epic:b re-asks b in round 2
- - §9 row 17: no regression prompt after a clean unedited round 2, one after a fixed resolution
tasks.closed_reason:
- Section 9 row 7: engine.EpicReviewCarry (internal/engine/epiccarry.go) carries a unit whose hash equals the round before's snapshot and that has no open row; over --milestone A on the chain round 2 asks no unit, emits no prompts and its next_action says to record an empty file, and after editing the why of b -> c round 3 asks exactly epic:a and epic:b with c as context and d by id only, verified by TestEpicReview_UnchangedUnitsAreCarried (internal/cli/epic_review_carry_test.go), red before the carry existed
- Section 9 row 18: a round-1 medium row on epic:b with no accepting disposition re-asks b in round 2 although its hash is unchanged, verified by TestEpicReview_AnOpenFindingReasksItsUnit (internal/cli/epic_review_carry_test.go)
- Section 9 row 17 with D2: regression is appended (internal/cli/epic_review_prompt.go epicRegressionPrompt) only when a unit hash changed or the round before holds a fixed row; a round-2 row resolved wontfix gives round 3 no regression prompt, and the same row resolved fixed re-asks epic:a and appends regression naming the fixed finding, verified by TestEpicReview_RegressionFollowsAFixedResolution (internal/cli/epic_review_carry_test.go)
